history.summary: A 1967 99-year leasehold 3BR walk-up (1,087 sqft) in Tiong Bahru, asking $999k ($919 psf) — by far the cheapest entry in the batch and on the cost frontier. Low absolute price and Tiong Bahru desirability are real, but a near-60-year-old leasehold carries heavy lease-decay and financing risk.
history.rating_rationale: At $999k / $919 psf this is a genuinely low entry price for prime-fringe Tiong Bahru, 450m from Havelock TEL MRT, which is why it sits on the frontier. But built 1967 on a 99-yr lease leaves ~40 years, triggering CPF/financing limits that shrink the buyer pool, and walk-ups carry no facilities. The cheap price partially offsets lease risk for a cash buyer/landlord; not for a leveraged investor. A speculative low-ticket hold, balanced — Neutral.
red_flags: 1967 build on 99-yr lease — ~40 yrs left, CPF/financing restrictions, lease decay
No URA data to confirm pricing or appreciation
Lease tail caps the holding horizon and exit options
catalysts: Low $999k absolute entry — cash-buyer / landlord friendly
En-bloc/SERS optionality for older Tiong Bahru blocks (speculative)

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Tiong Bahru rents strongly to lifestyle tenants; on a $999k basis the gross yield can be attractive (~4%+) even for a walk-up, the main investment merit here.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Lease decay is the dominant drag; capital upside depends on en-bloc/redevelopment optionality rather than organic appreciation. Rental carry, not capital growth, is the case.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Lease-decay constrained; low base price offers some cushion, en-bloc optionality speculative
